data.narrative:
Wetstone is a seed-stage company in the Climate & Energy sector. The comparable universe comprises one public company (LNZA) and eight private peers including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix. However, this peer set presents significant measurement constraints.

The peer-median method is inapplicable to Wetstone's valuation. Among the eight same-sector private comparables identified, zero operate at the seed stage, zero at adjacent stages, and zero fall within a similar valuation tier. This lack of sufficiently tight peer clustering—the analysis requires a minimum of three datapoints to establish a credible median—means any extrapolation from broader sector medians would introduce unacceptable distortion. The single public comparable spans a different development phase and market context than an early-stage private company.

Without a viable triangulation methodology, this analysis cannot responsibly estimate a valuation range. The core constraint is sparse data at the seed stage within Climate & Energy; the peer set, while populated, lacks the narrow-stage and tier-matching density required for quantitative comparison. Future valuation work should either (1) identify additional seed-stage Climate & Energy companies to establish statistical validity, or (2) apply alternative methods such as venture-capital method sizing based on exit scenarios and fund return requirements. Current data supports deferring point estimates until either methodology becomes defensible.
